decisionsTitle: «Vii mâine la …?»: the day before a ticked run, the newsletter's subscribers are asked by email, and one tap answers
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-18 01:00–01:20**, building on «Vin!» (§812): «I need this "Going" to be via email or something … super easy». §812 gave the event's page, the token page and the count; this adds the channel where nobody has to open the site: the club's newsletter asks, and one tap answers.

**Decision.** The day before an event the club ticked «Vin!» on, the confirmed newsletter subscribers who chose the topic **«Întrebarea «Vii?» înaintea alergărilor»** (`RSVP_ASK`) — or «Toate noutățile», which has always meant every topic, today's and any added later — get ONE email, «Vii mâine la <eveniment>?», with the event's facts block (§392), the event's calendar file, the newsletter's own way out, and two buttons: **«Vin»** counts them at once, **«Nu vin»** counts nobody. It builds on §812 and changes none of its rules: an answer is still not a registration (no place, no declaration, no participant; the allocator, the registrations and the capacity formula never meet it), the gate is still `rsvpOffered` (so the privacy notice in force must name `{{rsvp}}` in both languages), a name is still public only by the person's own tick.

**A topic of its own, not «Alergările săptămânale» (amends §513, §445).** The new-event alert's topic for a group run says in its hint «o dată pe serie, nu la fiecare alergare» — a subscriber who chose it was promised one message per series — so a question before every run would break what they were told. `RSVP_ASK` is added to the `newsletter_topic` enum (migration 0170, expand only; the value is appended last), offered in the pop-up and on the subscriber's own page like the others, and **off until ticked** (an existing subscription to everything receives it, by definition). It is an `AUTOMATIC_TOPICS` member: no organizer composes a newsletter under it (the composer, `SENDABLE_TOPICS` and the per-topic counts leave it out), because what the subscriber chose is a question with two answers. The privacy notice's `{{newsletterTopics}}` names it once a notice is approved from the template; one approved before does not, so the SETUP step says to approve again.

**When, once (amends §775).** `queueRsvpAsks(db, now)` is a step of the maintenance job beside `queueNewEventAlerts`. It asks an event on the club's calendar day BEFORE the day its start falls on (Europe/Bucharest — never «24 hours before», which is the wrong day twice a year; the 08:00 hour sits between the two changes of the clock and midnight is never inside one, so both are found on the wall clock with `fromWallTimeInput`), at the first run at or after **08:00 club time** (the morning of §775's digest: nothing at 03:00) and until the midnight that opens the event's day. So an event at 10:00 on Sunday is asked on Saturday from 08:00; one at 00:30 on Sunday is asked on Saturday from 08:00 too; **one ticked only on the day itself is never asked** (its window closed at midnight, and a question about «tomorrow» on the day would be a lie — the page's «Vin!» still takes the answer); one ticked at 22:00 the evening before is asked at the first run after the save. The event's row in `event_rsvp_asks` — UNIQUE on the event — is the «once», written in the same transaction as the messages; an event with nobody to ask still gets its row (a subscriber who joins tomorrow is not asked about today's event). A cancelled, unticked, registering, draft, undated or members-only event (§552) is never asked and gets no row; a cancelled event's row, once written, stays, so it is not asked a second time if put back the same day. Whoever already has a **confirmed** answer to the event (compared on the canonical address, AGENTS.md §10.4) is not asked. Because the job sleeps when nothing is due (§334), `nextMaintenanceWork` now includes each such event's window opening, or the job would sleep through the morning. The retention sweep deletes the row with the event's other rows, thirty days after its end (and not at a cancellation, for the reason above); it holds an event id and a count, nothing personal.

**The two links are §812's, not a new kind.** The message is queued with the subscriber's id and the event's, nothing secret. When it is **sent** (`prepareRsvpAsk`, called by the renderer, AGENTS.md §14.5) the subscriber's «Vin!» row for the event is made — unconfirmed, no name, no tick, `asked_at` set — and the existing `RSVP_CONFIRM` and `RSVP_WITHDRAW` links are minted for it by `mintRsvpLinks`; only their SHA-256 is kept, they work once, «Vin» for 48 hours (never past the start), «Nu vin» until the start. Both buttons open the token page of §812 (`/vin/<link>`, `/en/coming/<link>`) whose GET changes nothing (BR-REQ-036-02 criterion 4: a mail scanner opens every link first); the press is a POST. «Vin» is `confirmRsvp` — the personal link is the proof of the address, so it is a verified press (the `link` source of `identity.ts`): counted at once, no second email, the browser remembered for a year as for any press of a link. «Nu vin» is `withdrawRsvp` on the same row: it is deleted, the person is simply not on the list, and the page says «Bine, nu te numărăm. Poți răspunde altfel până la start.» **What was extended in the §812 rules, and nothing else:** `confirmRsvp` takes the optional name and the tick, applied only to a row the email made (`asked_at`), still unconfirmed and still nameless, so a name typed by someone on the page is never replaced and a counted row is never renamed; the link read (`readRsvpLink`) says whether the answer was asked and named; the page of the links shows, for an asked row only, the same box «Numele tău (opțional)» and the tick «Vreau să apar cu numele» as the event page's card under the one button, and the asked-specific words for «Nu vin». The newsletter's row has no name, so a one-tap «Vin» counts the person with no name and no tick — a name nobody typed is never made up.

**Taking over an unconfirmed row.** If the address was typed on the page and its own «Da, vin» email is still unused, the ask takes the row over: the name and the tick on it were typed by whoever typed the address (§812: an unconfirmed row never lends a stranger's name to a verified press), so they are cleared; the older confirm link dies with the new one; the row's age restarts, so the seven days of an unanswered row count from this email. A message whose reason is gone by the time it is sent — the subscriber unsubscribed, the address already counted, the event cancelled, unticked, given a registration, made the members', started, or the notice no longer naming «Vin!» — is withdrawn (`OutboxMessageWithdrawn`), not failed (§331).

**The road.** The message type `RSVP_ASK` (audience public, rendered by the newsletter's renderer so it carries the newsletter's manage link and privacy line) leaves by the **announcements'** road, as §812's confirmation does, **not** the newsletter's bulk road: a bulk row waits for the plan's allowance, last in line, and a question worth something only on the day before could arrive after the start. No club copy is queued for it (an automatic question, not a message about a person), and `/admin/emails` carries a card for it whose «când» line reads the hour from the one constant (`RSVP_ASK_CLOCK`).

**Open for the owner and the lawyer.** (1) The notice's newsletter paragraph and `{{newsletterTopics}}`: a notice approved before the topic existed does not name it; a lawyer reads the paragraph when it is approved again. (2) A subscriber ticked for «Toate noutățile» gets this question for every ticked event — one email per event, so two ticked events on the same day are two emails; the club decides how often to tick weekly runs. (3) The «Nu vin» press remembers the browser for a year, as §812's «Nu mai vin» does (its open point stands). (4) Until a subscriber presses or the seven days pass, the editor's read-only fold of answers lists each asked subscriber as an unconfirmed row (the Organizer and the Administrator see addresses there); the fold is not changed here. (5) `/admin/emails`' list of what will be sent does not forecast the question yet.

**Refused.** A new token table or a new link purpose (the existing two are exactly «Vin» and «Nu vin»); counting a typed or guessed address (the link is minted for a confirmed subscriber's own address, at the send); sending the question through the newsletter's bulk road; reusing «Alergările săptămânale» (it promised once per series); asking on the day itself; asking someone already counted; a composer choice for the topic; and a club copy of every ask.
changelogLine: - **«Vii mâine la …?» by email** — the day before a ticked run, from 08:00 club time, the newsletter's subscribers of the new topic «Întrebarea «Vii?» înaintea alergărilor» get one email with **«Vin»** (counted at once, with an optional name) and **«Nu vin»** (counted nowhere), once per event. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given the «Vii mâine la …?» email (`RSVP_ASK`), when it is queued, then its payload names only the subscriber and the event; when it is sent, then its two links are minted for the subscriber's own «Vin!» row (`RSVP_CONFIRM` and `RSVP_WITHDRAW`), only their hashes are stored, a newer message's links supersede them, no link carries the address, a GET of either changes nothing, «Vin» counts the subscriber on the press and «Nu vin» deletes the row so nobody is counted, and a message whose event, subscriber or notice no longer allows it is withdrawn rather than sent (2026-10-18, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

batchLine: the day before a ticked run, the newsletter's subscribers are asked «Vii?» with one-tap «Vin» / «Nu vin» links
